# Upstream unfinished surface

**Generated by `Tools/gen-monotodo-inventory.ps1` - do not edit by hand.**

This port compiles Mono's sources in place, so it inherits their unfinished members as well as
their finished ones. Two markers count here, and they mean different things:

| Marker | What it means for a caller |
|---|---|
| `[MonoTODO]` | A note from the original author. The member may work, may work partially, or may be a stub that silently returns `null`. **It does not throw**, which is what makes it the dangerous one. |
| `throw new NotImplementedException` | The member is a placeholder. You find out on the first call, loudly. |

Neither is a defect in this port, and neither is a to-do list for it: they are a map of where
upstream stopped. `LIMITATIONS.md` documents what the port deliberately changed; this file
documents what it deliberately did not touch.

A silently-null `[MonoTODO]` stub is exactly how Dynamic Data's field templates rendered blank
cells on a page returning HTTP 200 - worth remembering when a member returns nothing and no
error appears.

**Scope.** Only files that reach the compiler through a `Sources.generated.props` are counted -
upstream sources and their line-preserving patched copies. Code written FOR this port
(`Port/`, `Shims/`, `Overrides/`) is excluded, and so is anything dropped by
`Tools/port-exclusions.txt`: a stub nobody can reach is not a hazard. So a project can show zero
here and still have members this port chose not to implement - those are in `LIMITATIONS.md`.

## How to check one member

The counts say where to be careful; they do not say which member. To check a specific one, read
the upstream source - it is in the tree, and the port did not move it:

```powershell
Select-String -Path Mono/mcs/class/System.Web/**/*.cs -Pattern 'MonoTODO' -Context 0,3 |
    Where-Object { $_.Context.PostContext -match 'YourMemberName' }
```

If it throws, you will know at once. If it is a stub, the give-away is an auto-property with a
private setter that nothing in the file ever assigns.
